podcasts.title: Replay: Principles and Algorithms for Work and Life | Ray Dalio (2019)
podcasts.description:
Can you turn the lessons you learn from experience into a repeatable system for making better decisions? Ray Dalio argues that writing down the principles behind your decisions, testing them against history, and eventually turning them into algorithms can help.

In this archive conversation, Ray joins a16z’s Alex Rampell and Sonal Chokshi to discuss decision-making under uncertainty, learning from mistakes, and why understanding cause and effect matters more than blindly trusting a black-box model.

They also get into radical open-mindedness, judging people on process rather than outcomes, building teams around complementary strengths, and why knowing what you don’t know may be more valuable than what you do.

podcasts.title: Building a chip to beat biology | Naveen Rao - Unconventional AI  [Tape Out - Ep.001]
podcasts.description:
"We actually build chips every three months. Like we literally tape out a new chip."

Naveen Rao has built two AI companies and sold them both: Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third, Unconventional AI, looks nothing like either of them.

His argument is that AI is now limited by energy, so the number that matters is joules per token. Getting there means dropping the von Neumann split between memory and compute and building a machine that is "programmed by weights." To learn fast, his team tapes out a new chip roughly every three months. Their first test chip, a system of coupled oscillators, generated small images at about 900 nanojoules each, against about 50 millijoules on a GPU.

Dylan Patel pushes on all of it:
- why so many analog chips blew their lead once you count the conversion costs
- whether programmability still matters when NVIDIA is king
- whether we will stop buying computers and start buying intelligence tokens
- how far AI can go in designing chips itself

Tape Out is a new SemiAnalysis series: we sit across from the founders building AI hardware and ask the hard questions.

podcasts.title: The brain helped us build AI. Now AI is explaining the brain.
podcasts.description:
The human brain remains one of the greatest unsolved mysteries in science. We have roughly 86 billion neurons firing in a way that somehow produces intelligence, and yet the brain is still largely a black box. In the early days of AI, researchers looked to the brain for clues about how to build smarter machines. But today, that relationship has been flipped on its head. Join Professor Hannah Fry and neuroscience researchers Maria Eckstein and Kim Stachenfeld to see how scientists are using AI to better understand the human mind. podcasts.title: Scott Wu on Cybersecurity, Compute, and the Future of Engineering - [Invest Like the Best, EP.502]
podcasts.description:
Scott Wu is the CEO and co-founder of Cognition, the company behind the AI coding agent Devin.

Cognition made its first dollar of revenue in September 2024. Less than two years later, it crossed a $1 billion run rate, and Citi is rolling Devin out to about 14,000 engineers as it brings software projects in-house. We talk about what that means for the job of an engineer, and the trade-off between buying too much compute and not having enough to serve your customers. 

Scott thinks major breaches at some of the world's largest companies and government agencies are almost inevitable in the next six to 12 months. As AI agents start working in swarms, they're finding flaws that have gone unnoticed for years. I ask him what companies should be doing now and why he still thinks the attackers will lose in the long run. 

Please enjoy my conversation with Scott Wu.

podcasts.title: REPLAY: The Story of Apple Pay | Jennifer Bailey (2024)
podcasts.description:
When Apple Pay launched in the U.S., only about 3% of merchants accepted contactless payments. A decade later, Jennifer Bailey has helped expand it to 75 markets and more than 11,000 bank and network partners.

Jennifer joins a16z General Partner Alex Rampell to tell the story of building Apple Pay, from solving the chicken-and-egg problem of banks, merchants, and consumers to designing payments around security and privacy without Apple seeing individual transactions.

They also discuss the expansion from payments into transit, tickets, car and hotel keys, and digital IDs, plus why customer experience, patience, and timing have shaped Jennifer’s approach to building new products inside Apple.

podcasts.title: The One-Person Biotech | OpenAI Life Sciences
podcasts.description:
What happens when scientists are no longer limited by human attention? OpenAI’s Joy Jiao and Ashoka Rajendra join a16z’s Jay Rughani and Jorge Conde to discuss how AI and thousands of parallel agents could reshape drug discovery and development.

They trace OpenAI’s life sciences work from scientific reasoning to the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, and how agents could search biological data, manage clinical trials, and navigate regulatory and manufacturing workflows.

They also discuss AI’s role in solving difficult diagnoses and a future where a single person could potentially launch and advance multiple biotech programs.
